newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy MIF futures market launches new derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Italy MIF futures market launches new derivatives.

text.p: The Italian futures market (MIF) said it plans to introduce a futures contract on the one-month RIBOR rate, and the government bond market (MTS) is launching a secondary market for repo tenders on Treasury bonds.
The MTS and MIF management committee made the announcement in a statement after a meeting with representatives of the Treasury, the Bank of Italy and stock market regulatory authority Consob.
The measures must now be approved by the Treasury.

For the RIBOR (Rome Interbank Offered Rate) future, the dealing unit will be of three billion lire, delivery will be monthly and the last day of trading will be two working days preceding the third Wednesday of each month.
The price will be 100 minus the interest rate.
Minimum movement will be one basis point and the minimum quotation by market makers will be of 10 lots. There will be three expiries quoted and trading will be carried out between 0750 and 1610 GMT.
Ministerial sources said they expected the new contract to be launched soon.

MTS said the new repo market would facilitate the availability of paper and the covering of positions as well as guaranteeing transparency and efficiency with respect to the existing "over the counter" market which has developed, especially abroad.
